sentences.en: When did Cleo and Elsa get involved in the Girl Scouts?

sentences.en: I think we signed them up for Girl Scouts when they were six or seven.

sentences.en: So, there's the Girl Scout promise, and then there's also the Girl Scout law.
sentences.zh: 所以，有女童军誓词，然后还有女童军守则。

sentences.en: Okay, so it's, On my honor, I will try to serve God and my country, to help people at all times, and to live by the Girl Scout law.
sentences.zh: 好吧，内容是：凭我的荣誉，我保证竭尽所能，效忠上帝和祖国，随时随地帮助他人，并遵守女童军守则。

sentences.en: I will do my best to be honest and fair, friendly and helpful, considerate and caring, courageous and strong, and responsible for what I say and do,

sentences.en: and to respect myself and others, respect authority, use resources wisely, make the world a better place, and be a sister to every Girl Scout.

sentences.en: Yeah, that's one of the reasons I did it, but then they just got kind of, meh.

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: Yeah, we mostly just made, like, stuff out of beads and colored in coloring pages, quote-unquote girlish crafts.

sentences.en: I don't like that term.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢那个词。

sentences.en: Where do you think that these ideas come from, of what girlish and boyish mean?
sentences.zh: 你觉得关于女孩气和男孩气含义的这些想法是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: I think they come from, like, a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们是很久以前传下来的。

sentences.en: Girls were assigned to do certain things, more like stay-at-home things, and boys were assigned to more, like, go out to war and be heroes.
sentences.zh: 女孩被分配去做某些事情，更像是呆在家里的事情，而男孩被分配去更多地参军打仗并成为英雄。

sentences.en: In the old days, they, like, they were told they were supposed to wear dresses,
sentences.zh: 在过去，她们被告知应该穿裙子，

sentences.en: so people have kind of started to put, like, dresses and girls together and, like, boys and strong together.
sentences.zh: 所以人们有点开始把裙子和女孩联系在一起，把男孩和坚强联系在一起。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Beautiful.

sentences.en: And then maybe another time, there's an ad for Nerf guns, and the only actors are boys, and it's saying, like, boys, grab your Nerf guns and go.
sentences.zh: 然后也许在另一个时间，有一个关于Nerf枪的广告，唯一的演员都是男孩，它说的是，男孩们，抓起你们的Nerf枪出发吧。

sentences.en: And I'm like, why are there no girls in there?
sentences.zh: 我就想，为什么里面没有女孩？

sentences.en: Because this is how we play it.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是我们的玩法。

sentences.en: Nerf Elite, Fire Strike, Disruptor, and Retaliator.
sentences.zh: Nerf精英系列，火击发射器、破坏者和复仇者。

sentences.en: Batteries not included.
sentences.zh: 不含电池。

sentences.en: Each sold separately.
sentences.zh: 单独出售。

sentences.en: It sounds like you've given a lot of thought to this.
sentences.zh: 听起来你对此思考了很多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I wasn't actually as concerned about it until third grade, and then I started to think about, like, how I was not being the way people expected me to be.
sentences.zh: 我其实直到三年级才这么关注，然后我开始思考，我怎么没有表现出人们期望我有的样子。

sentences.en: And I've had, like, classmates in school say, like, why are you wearing boy clothes, or why do you have boy hair?
sentences.zh: 而且我在学校里遇到过同班同学说，你为什么穿男孩的衣服，或者你为什么留男孩的头发？

sentences.en: That means you're a boy.
sentences.zh: 那就意味着你是个男孩。

sentences.en: I think the turning point for Elsa was that we sent, two summers ago, we sent both girls to a Girl Scout camp, a day camp.
sentences.zh: 我觉得埃尔莎的转折点是，我们在两年前的夏天，把两个女孩都送去参加了一个女童军日间夏令营。

sentences.en: And Elsa had a really hard time there.
sentences.zh: 埃尔莎在那里过得很艰难。

sentences.en: It was the same summer that she cut her hair, and some kids asked her, why are you going to Girl Scout camp?
sentences.zh: 那是她剪头发的同一个夏天，一些孩子问她，你为什么来女童军夏令营？

sentences.en: They thought she was a boy, and wanted to know why there was a boy going with them to Girl Scout camp.
sentences.zh: 他们以为她是个男孩，想知道为什么会有一个男孩和他们一起去女童军夏令营。

sentences.en: She kind of got in arguments with other girls.
sentences.zh: 她跟其他女孩吵过架。

sentences.en: She got in arguments with the leadership, and she was visibly unhappy.
sentences.zh: 她跟领导层也吵过架，而且她明显很不开心。

sentences.en: And that was the end of her Girl Scouting career.
sentences.zh: 那是她女童军生涯的结束。

sentences.en: So, I just thought, well, if I don't want Girl Scouts, why can't a girl be in Boy Scouts?
sentences.zh: 所以，我当时想，如果我不想要女童军，为什么女孩不能加入男童军呢？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I had heard that there are more activities I like, like archery and whittling and horseback riding, but they don't actually do horseback riding.
sentences.zh: 我听说那里有更多我喜欢的活动，比如射箭、削木片和骑马，但他们实际上并不骑马。

sentences.en: That's fine, though.
sentences.zh: 不过没关系。

sentences.en: So, things that were a little more adventurous sounding.
sentences.zh: 所以，是一些听起来更有冒险精神的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, Elsa came to us last year and said, I want to be a Boy Scout.
sentences.zh: 对啊，埃尔莎去年找到我们，说她想成为一名童子军。

sentences.en: And our first response was to say, well, that's not possible.
sentences.zh: 而我们的第一反应是，这不可能。

sentences.en: When I asked my dad, and he said, well, they probably won't let you in because you're a girl.
sentences.zh: 当我问我爸爸时，他说，嗯，他们可能不会让你进去，因为你是女孩。

sentences.en: I said, well, then I can just sneak in and pretend I'm a boy because of my hair.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，那我可以偷偷溜进去，因为我的头发假装自己是个男孩。

sentences.en: Still, up until just a few weeks ago, the rule in the Boy Scouts was that girls weren't allowed.
sentences.zh: 尽管直到几周前，童子军的规矩还是不允许女孩加入。

sentences.en: But as it turns out, we know the guy who runs the troop, so he'll probably let me in.
sentences.zh: 但结果证明，我们认识管理这个小队的负责人，所以他可能会让我加入。

sentences.en: That means I can get in.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我能进去了。

sentences.en: Probably.
sentences.zh: 大概吧。

sentences.en: What the scout leaders in our local troop told us was that while they couldn't register Elsa with the national organization,
sentences.zh: 我们当地小队的童子军领队告诉我们，虽然他们不能在国家组织为埃尔莎注册，

sentences.en: they could sign her up.
sentences.zh: 但他们可以给她报名。

sentences.en: They would get her a uniform.
sentences.zh: 他们会给她一套制服。

sentences.en: She could earn all the badges that all the other boys earned.
sentences.zh: 她可以获得其他所有男孩能获得的所有徽章。

sentences.en: And for all intents and purposes, she would be a Boy Scout.
sentences.zh: 而且从各方面来看，她就是一名童子军。

sentences.en: And that's the way it's been.
sentences.zh: 事情一直以来就是这样的。

sentences.en: What's the scout host?
sentences.zh: 童子军的赞助机构是什么？

sentences.en: Could you say it for me?
sentences.zh: 你能帮我说一下吗？

sentences.en: Um, I can't exactly remember.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记不太清了。

sentences.en: Can I get, it says it on my scouting book.
sentences.zh: 我能拿一下吗，我的童子军手册上有写。

sentences.en: Can I get that really quickly?
sentences.zh: 我能马上去拿一下吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Okay, I'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 好的，我马上回来。

sentences.en: Please, please hold.
sentences.zh: 请，请稍候。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: You know how sometimes it seems like your kid actually knows more than you?
sentences.zh: 你知道有时感觉你的孩子其实比你懂得还多吗？

sentences.en: Get ready for more of that.
sentences.zh: 准备好迎接更多这样的时刻吧。

sentences.en: Because thanks to the Google Assistant, Google Home Mini is great for adulting.
sentences.zh: 因为有了谷歌助理，谷歌智能音箱迷你版对于成年生活大有帮助。

sentences.en: But it's also great for the rest of the family.
sentences.zh: 但对于家里的其他人也同样很有用。

sentences.en: Watch this.
sentences.zh: 看这个。

sentences.en: Hey Google, play space trivia.
sentences.zh: 嘿，谷歌，播放太空问答。

sentences.en: What's at the middle of the Milky Way galaxy?
sentences.zh: 银河系的中心有什么？

sentences.en: A black hole.
sentences.zh: 一个黑洞。

sentences.en: Yep, definitely didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我绝对不知道这个。

sentences.en: Just add your kid's Google account, powered by Family Link, and ask it to do even more stuff.
sentences.zh: 只需添加你孩子的谷歌账户（由家庭链接支持），然后让它做更多的事情。

sentences.en: From choose-your-own-adventure stories to musical chairs.
sentences.zh: 从自主选择历险故事到抢椅子游戏。

sentences.en: And when you're done listening to this podcaSt...
sentences.zh: 当你听完这个播客之后……

sentences.en: Hey Google, play the Kids Daily podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嘿，谷歌，播放儿童日报播客。

sentences.en: Here's the latest news from the Daily for Kids.
sentences.zh: 以下是儿童日报的最新消息。

sentences.en: It's family time, like only Google can.
sentences.zh: 这是属于全家的时间，只有谷歌能做到。

sentences.en: Okay, I got it.
sentences.zh: 好的，我找到了。

sentences.en: Okay, oh, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，哦，谢谢你。

sentences.en: So could you recite the pledge for me?
sentences.zh: 那你呢，能为我背诵一下誓词吗？

sentences.en: Okay, well, the Scout Oath is,
sentences.zh: 好的，嗯，童子军誓词是：

sentences.en: On my honor, I will do my best to do my duty to God and my country and to obey the Scout law,
sentences.zh: 在我的荣誉下，我将竭尽全力履行我对上帝和国家的职责，遵守童子军法律，

sentences.en: to help other people at all times, to keep myself physically strong, mentally awake, and morally straight.
sentences.zh: 随时帮助他人，保持身体强健、头脑清醒、品格正直。

sentences.en: I remember the first day.
sentences.zh: 我还记得第一天。

sentences.en: I was pretty nervous.
sentences.zh: 我当时挺紧张的。

sentences.en: I walked in, and I was kind of like going slowly, and I kind of had my head down a little.
sentences.zh: 我走进去，动作有点慢，还稍微有点低着头。

sentences.en: Even though I knew people would think I was a boy at first, I was so kind of shy about it.
sentences.zh: 尽管我知道一开始大家会以为我是个男孩，但我对此还是感到很害羞。

sentences.en: There were a few misunderstandings.
sentences.zh: 有一些小误解。

sentences.en: The other boys in the troop were kind of like, oh, they looked at me a little, like a little strangely,
sentences.zh: 小队里的其他男孩有点像，哦，他们看了我一眼，有点奇怪的眼神，

sentences.en: just like if you like, like if someone is wearing like a weird hat, kind of like the way you look at them, like, oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 就像如果你喜欢，就像如果有人戴了一顶奇怪的帽子，你看着他们的那种眼神，就像，哦，好吧。

sentences.en: They definitely knew that I was there, so I felt like, well, I have to introduce myself, and I'm going to be brave about it, and I can do it.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对知道我在那里，所以我心想，嗯，我得自我介绍一下，我要勇敢一点，我能做到。

sentences.en: That's kind of what I thought.
sentences.zh: 我当时就是这么想的。

sentences.en: My name is Dylan Bates, um, I'm 10 years old, and I'm from Melrose, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 我叫迪伦·贝茨，嗯，我10岁，我来自马萨诸塞州梅尔罗斯。

sentences.en: My name is Harry Kregelski, I'm 10 years old, and I'm from Melrose, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 我叫哈里·克雷格尔斯基，我10岁，我来自马萨诸塞州梅尔罗斯。

sentences.en: Harry and Dylan are in Elsa's troop.
sentences.zh: 哈里和迪伦在埃尔莎的小队里。

sentences.en: Not to be that mean, but she usually is the boss for things, and something that she's pretty, she's really good at is like,
sentences.zh: 不是故意说得那么苛刻，但她通常是各种事情的主心骨，她非常擅长的一点是，

sentences.en: one week there was this thing where you would go to this camp, and there was this one day where we would make these forts with sticks,
sentences.zh: 有那么一周，我们去了一个夏令营，有一天我们要用树枝搭建堡垒，

sentences.en: and Elsa, basically, she was like the director for everything, because there was this one part where we would take moss and put it on the bottom of the fort,
sentences.zh: 基本上埃尔莎就是所有事情的总指挥，因为有一个环节我们要拿苔藓铺在堡垒底部，

sentences.en: and it would act like a cushion.
sentences.zh: 这样它就能起到垫子的作用。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: It was her idea.
sentences.zh: 这是她的主意。

sentences.en: Do you remember a moment, Elsa, where you felt like the boys in the troop accepted you?
sentences.zh: 埃尔莎，你还记得什么时候觉得小队里的男孩们接纳了你吗？

sentences.en: Well, I was, this is actually something very recent, just the last PAC meeting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是，这其实是很近的事，就在上一次家长委员会会议上。

sentences.en: I was actually elected patrol leader, kind of like the leader of the troop for the rest of the year, and I was really happy when they decided me.
sentences.zh: 我实际上被选为巡逻队队长，有点像今年剩余时间里小队的领袖，当他们选定我时我真的很高兴。

sentences.en: That's a big deal.
sentences.zh: 这可是件大事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: Hello, this is Dylan.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是迪伦。

sentences.en: If anyone is just secretly telling her, like, well, you a boy scout, just why?
sentences.zh: 如果有人悄悄对她说，嗯，你是个童子军，为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why would you do that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Because, you know what?
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Elsa can do lots of things, and it takes lots of bravery to step up and be a leader,
sentences.zh: 埃尔莎能做很多事情，站出来成为领导者需要很大的勇气，

sentences.en: because lots of people do want to be a leader, but it takes true bravery to be a real leader.
sentences.zh: 因为很多人都想成为领导者，但要成为真正的领导者需要真正的勇气。

sentences.en: Well, Dylan and Harry, thank you both for your time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，迪伦和哈里，非常感谢你们抽出时间。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: Oh, you're welcome.
sentences.zh: 哦，不客气。

sentences.en: So, Elsa, how important do you think it is for someone like you to have the choice between the Boy Scouts and the Girl Scouts?
sentences.zh: 那么，埃尔莎，你认为像你这样的人有权在童子军和女童子军之间做出选择有多重要？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's important for me to have a choice, because I know if I didn't have a choice,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为对我来说有选择权很重要，因为我知道如果没有选择权，

sentences.en: I would be stuck with something I didn't enjoy,
sentences.zh: 我就会被困在我不喜欢的事情上，

sentences.en: and if no one had ever had a choice,
sentences.zh: 而且如果从来没有人有过选择权，

sentences.en: that
sentences.zh: 那

sentences.en: we wouldn't be where we are today,
sentences.zh: 我们就不会有今天，

sentences.en: I probably wouldn't be the way I am now,
sentences.zh: 我也可能不会是现在这个样子，

sentences.en: and I enjoy the way I am now, so I think it's very important that I had that choice.
sentences.zh: 而且我很喜欢现在的自己，所以我认为能有这种选择非常重要。

sentences.en: Cleo here.
sentences.zh: 克莱奥到。

sentences.en: This is my sash.
sentences.zh: 这是我的绶带。

sentences.en: It's pretty nice.
sentences.zh: 挺不错的。

sentences.en: I got some of them badges.
sentences.zh: 我有一些这样的徽章。

sentences.en: So, cookie sale, which is what the Girl Scouts always do, which is one of my favorite things about Girl Scouts.
sentences.zh: 所以，卖饼干，这是女童子军一直在做的，也是我最喜欢女童子军的地方之一。

sentences.en: Cleo, when your sister joined the Boy Scouts, you chose to stay in the Girl Scouts.
sentences.zh: 克莱奥，当你的姐姐加入童子军时，你选择留在女童子军。

sentences.en: What do you like about it?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢它什么？

sentences.en: Well, I don't, like, hate boys, but I do like to get away with just girls for a little bit, because boys do fool around a lot, and sometimes it's a little annoying,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我倒不是讨厌男孩，但我确实喜欢偶尔只有女孩在一起，因为男孩们总是胡闹，有时候有点烦人，

sentences.en: and sometimes they're a little distracting, so I like doing stuff with just girls and just my friends that are girls.
sentences.zh: 而且有时候他们有点让人分心，所以我喜欢只和女孩以及我那些女孩朋友一起做事情。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But I'd really like to do some more cool stuff, because, like, the Boy Scouts get to do, like, wood cutting and obstacle courses,
sentences.zh: 但我真的很想做更多酷炫的事情，因为，比如，童子军可以做砍树和障碍训练之类的，

sentences.en: and the Girl Scouts doesn't really do much of that.
sentences.zh: 而女童子军基本上不做这些。

sentences.en: Boy Scouts goes out and does, like, really, like, cool, like, crafts, like, they rock, they launch, like, mini rockets and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 童子军会出去做一些，真的，很酷的，比如手工，他们会发射迷你火箭之类的东西。

sentences.en: Five, four, three, two, one.
sentences.zh: 五，四，三，二，一。

sentences.en: Oh, that one is a higher one.
sentences.zh: 哦，那个飞得更高。

sentences.en: Clear, you seem a little envious of what the Boy Scouts do.
sentences.zh: 克莱奥，你似乎有点嫉妒童子军做的事情。

sentences.en: Am I sensing that?
sentences.zh: 是我感觉到了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I am a little envious,
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实有点嫉妒，

sentences.en: because they get to do slightly more exciting stuff than us, and they get to have, like, a pocket knife.
sentences.zh: 因为他们能做比我们稍微刺激一点的事情，而且他们还能拥有，比如一把折叠刀。

sentences.en: Do you want a pocket knife?
sentences.zh: 你想要一把折叠刀吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd say so.
sentences.zh: 对，我想是的。

sentences.en: That would be cool.
sentences.zh: 那一定很酷。

sentences.en: Do you think it would be better to bring in the activities that boys do into Girl Scouts instead of girls feeling like
sentences.zh: 你觉得把男孩们做的活动引入女童子军，会不会比让女孩们觉得

sentences.en: they have to leave Girl Scouts in order to do those activities?
sentences.zh: 为了做这些活动而不得不离开女童子军要好呢？

sentences.en: I do think that, because I do think girls can concentrate more around regular girls, but they would like to do the stuff that Boy Scouts does,
sentences.zh: 我确实这么觉得，因为我认为女孩在普通的女孩周围更能集中注意力，但她们又想做童子军做的事情，

sentences.en: so I think it would help if that stuff was brought into the Girl Scout troops.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为如果把那些活动引入女童子军小队会有所帮助。

sentences.en: So, do you feel like you can be more yourself, or that you learn more, when it's just girls?
sentences.zh: 那么，你觉得只有女孩在一起时，你能更好地做自己，或者能学到更多东西吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think I can sort of be more myself, because I feel like not as embarrassed around girls, sort of, like, they're more comfortable to talk with and stuff.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得我能在某种程度上更好地做自己，因为我觉得和女孩在一起时没那么尴尬，某种程度上，和她们交流更自在之类的。

sentences.en: Sometimes girls just need to concentrate, and they should be able to just be themselves when they're with their own gender.
sentences.zh: 有时候女孩们就是需要集中注意力，当她们和同性在一起时，应该能够做真正的自己。

sentences.en: Whew, how do you sum up daughters?
sentences.zh: 呼，怎么总结女儿这种生物呢？

sentences.en: They're a whole bundle of things, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 她们是一大堆复杂事物的集合体，对吧？

sentences.en: We have two very different girls, and they're completely their own kids, but to the extent they represent other girls, girls, I think they do leadership in different ways.
sentences.zh: 我们有两个截然不同的女孩，她们完全是独立的个体，但在她们代表其他女孩的程度上，我认为她们以不同的方式展现了领导力。

sentences.en: I'm sure that the girl-only spaces has been helpful to Cleo to some degree.
sentences.zh: 我确信纯女孩的空间在某种程度上对克莱奥很有帮助。

sentences.en: I can see times when she gets a little overshadowed by boys, and I think having a time, and it doesn't happen very often, she's in a co-ed school,
sentences.zh: 我能看出有时她会被男孩们掩盖光芒，我觉得拥有一段时间——虽然不常发生，她在男女同校的学校上学，

sentences.en: so that little bit of time once a week, or whatever it is, to hang out with just girls, and to be doing activities with other girls, I think it's probably been good for Cleo,
sentences.zh: 所以每周有那么一小段时间，或者不管什么时候，只和女孩们在一起，和其他女孩一起做活动，我认为对克莱奥来说可能挺好的，

sentences.en: and she seems happy with it.
sentences.zh: 而且她对此似乎也很高兴。

sentences.en: For Elsa, she wanted to be in the Boy Scouts, and she has her own reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 至于埃尔莎，她想加入童子军，她有她自己的理由。

sentences.en: It really comes down to what feels empowering to them.
sentences.zh: 这归根结底取决于什么能带给她们赋能的感觉。

sentences.en: Hey, Cleo and Elsa, can you hear me?
sentences.zh: 嘿，克莱奥和埃尔莎，你们能听到我说话吗？

sentences.en: Yeah!
sentences.zh: 能！

sentences.en: Okay, Boy Scouts won't start accepting girls until next year, but you two have been able to think about what this decision might mean earlier than most people.
sentences.zh: 好的，童子军要到明年才会开始接受女孩，但你们两个已经能够比大多数人更早地思考这个决定可能意味着什么。

sentences.en: You're kind of a glimpse into the future of what a lot of other girls across the country are going to get to think about soon.
sentences.zh: 你们就像是一瞥全国许多其他女孩不久后都要开始思考的未来。

sentences.en: If you could give advice to girls who are deciding whether to stay in Girl Scouts or join the Boy Scouts, what would you say to them?
sentences.zh: 如果你能给那些正在决定是留在女童子军还是加入童子军的女孩们一些建议，你会对她们说什么？

sentences.en: Okay, Cleo here.
sentences.zh: 好的，克莱奥发言。

sentences.en: If I were trying to persuade someone to stay in the Girl Scouts, I would probably say, well, like, there are a lot of really, really nice girls in the Girl Scouts,
sentences.zh: 如果我要试着说服某人留在女童子军，我可能会说，嗯，女童子军里有很多非常非常好的女孩，

sentences.en: and it's just, like,
sentences.zh: 而且就是，

sentences.en: I've always felt comfortable with these girls, especially since they're my friends, and it's just, we, like, the activities aren't always as cool as the ones in Boy Scouts,
sentences.zh: 我一直和这些女孩在一起感到很舒服，尤其是她们都是我的朋友，而且就是，我们，虽然活动不像童子军里的那么酷，

sentences.en: but we do do some pretty fun activities, and we have good times together, so that's fun.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实做一些挺好玩的活动，大家在一起也很开心，所以这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: Okay, Elsa, responding to the question.
sentences.zh: 好的，埃尔莎，来回答这个问题。

sentences.en: So I think a top reason why, wait, is why, like, a girl could join the Boy Scouts?
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得女孩加入童子军的一个主要原因，等等，就是为什么，

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Yeah, okay.
sentences.zh: 对，好吧。

sentences.en: Is because she wanted to.
sentences.zh: 是因为她想这样做。

sentences.en: Because she can.
sentences.zh: 因为她能行。

sentences.en: You can, so it's perfectly fine if you want to.
sentences.zh: 你可以这么做，所以如果你想的话完全没问题。

sentences.en: Um, I want to tell you both that I think you are really cool.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想对你们两个说，我觉得你们真的很酷。

sentences.en: You're great, you're smart, you're sensitive, and you're caring, and I'm really glad to have met you.
sentences.zh: 你们很棒，很聪明，很敏感，也很体贴，我很高兴能认识你们。

sentences.en: Thank ya.
sentences.zh: 谢谢啦。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Okey-pokey.
sentences.zh: 好嘞。

sentences.en: Sunday's edition of The Times features a special print section for kids that will be published every month starting next year.
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》周日版将推出一个专门的儿童印刷版块，从明年开始每月出版一次。

sentences.en: You can pick it up on newsstands or by subscribing for home delivery to The Times.
sentences.zh: 你可以在报摊上买到，或者通过订阅《泰晤士报》送货上门来获取。

sentences.en: The Kids Daily was produced by Lindsay Garrison with help from Franny Caratoth.
sentences.zh: 《儿童日报》由林赛·加里森制作，弗拉尼·卡拉托思协助。

sentences.en: Lisa Tobin is our executive producer.
sentences.zh: 丽莎·托宾是我们的执行制片人。

sentences.en: Samantha Hennig is our editorial director.
sentences.zh: 萨曼莎·赫尼格是我们的总编辑。

sentences.en: Brad Fisher is our technical manager.
sentences.zh: 布拉德·费舍尔是我们的技术经理。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 我们周一见。

sentences.en: But I don't get it.
sentences.zh: 但我不明白。

sentences.en: How come a girl can go and be a Boy Scout, but a boy can't be a Girl Scout?
sentences.zh: 为什么女孩可以去当童子军，而男孩却不能当女童子军？

sentences.en: So, would you want to have the option to do that?
sentences.zh: 那么，你想拥有这种选择的权力吗？

sentences.en: Well, this is Dylan.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这位是迪伦。

sentences.en: And having the option...
sentences.zh: 而且拥有这种选择……

sentences.en: I'm sorry, I got a sneeze.

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的政治机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称是改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场激烈、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的权力之争。
